DisplayText: So the decision I keep coming back to is whether we should have kept the queue at all. The original idea was that anything slow would go on the queue and the request would come back straight away, which sounded right at the time. What actually happened was that every failure moved somewhere nobody was looking. A request that used to fail in front of you now failed 20 minutes later in a worker log, and by then the person who caused it had gone home, so we pulled about half of it back inline. The requests got slower, which nobody enjoyed, but the every is came back to the person who could do something about them.
